sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:65

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:65:1
items.html:
Netzah and Hod, and they needed to come reign, etc., and their vessel descended into Netzah and Hod of Beria: It has already been explained above (page 537, the passage beginning “The light of Tifferet”) that according to the reason given here for the expansion of the three lines of KHB into HGT — namely, that the kings NHYM could not come out to their place because it was not vacant, since the lights of Daat and HGT were there — it turns out that at the time of the emergence of the kings NH the line of Bina expanded, so that the light of Gevura, which was in the place of the Sefirot NH, would rise there. And since the light of Gevura rose and became distant from the vessel, the vessel of Gevura fell to Yesod of Beria. Afterward Netzah and Hod reigned, and when they broke, NH descended to NH of Beria. And at the time of the emergence of the king Yesod, which did not find its place vacant, the line of Hochma had to expand, and the light of Hesed was raised there from the place of the Sefira of Yesod to the vessel of Hesed that was made from the expansion of Hochma. And through the distancing of the light of Hesed from the vessel, the vessel of Hesed fell to the place of Tifferet of Beria. Thus it turns out now that the vessel of Daat is in the Malchut of Beria, and above it the vessel of Gevura, and above it the vessel of Netzah and Hod, and above it the vessel of Hesed.
However, this is most puzzling: that the vessel of NH, which is of the last kings, whose breaking is not so great, should fall still below the vessel of Hesed, which is of the first kings, whose breaking is very great, since they were exposed without any clothing from the posterior of Ima, as above in the words of the ARI. We have already expanded on this above (on page 537), and it was explained there from the words of the ARI in most places that the expansion of the three lines of KHB is itself the matter of the fall of the posterior of AVI, and that this entire expansion was completed together with the completion of the fall of the posterior of AVI, that is, in the upper third of Tifferet. And after YESHSUT came out and clothed the posterior of AVI, immediately all four lights of HGT rose there to the new vessels of the expansion of KHB. Then all three vessels — Daat, Hesed and Gevura — descended together to the place of NHYM of Beria: Daat in Malchut, Hesed in Yesod, and Gevura in NH, that is, whichever is coarser than its fellow is below it, as above. And all this was before the emergence of the last kings into the vessels of NHYM of Atzilut, so that when the kings NHYM came to reign, their place was already vacant. Therefore they too fell into Beria in this order, that whichever is coarser than its fellow fell below its fellow, and therefore NH fell into Tifferet of Beria, the vessel of Yesod into Gevura of Beria, and the vessel of Malchut into Hesed of Beria.
Thus the seven kings are now found in the ZAT of Beria in the correct order, that whichever is more refined is above, since its breaking is not so great, and whichever is coarser is below, since its breaking is the greater. So that the vessel of Malchut is in Hesed of Beria, the vessel of Yesod is in Gevura of Beria, the vessel of NH is in Tifferet of Beria, the vessel of Gevura is in Netzah and Hod of Beria, the vessel of Hesed is in Yesod of Beria, and the vessel of Daat is in Malchut of Beria. The exception is the vessel of Tifferet, which did not descend to the ZAT of Beria but only to the Keter of Beria, for the reason explained above (page 538, the passage beginning “The upper half”), study it there well.
